title: Flat quotient with projective reduction gives split sequence of completions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $u:K\to E$ and $v:E\to M$ be $R$-linear maps such that $u$ is injective, $v$ is surjective, and $\operatorname{im}(u)=\ker(v)$. Assume $M$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $M/IM$ is projective over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For each $R$-module $L$, define $\widehat L=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}L/I^nL$ as the module of compatible residue classes with componentwise operations, where $I^nL$ is generated by $rx$ for $r\in I^n$, $x\in L$. Define $\widehat u:\widehat K\to\widehat E$ and $\widehat v:\widehat E\to\widehat M$ by applying the maps induced by $u$ and $v$ at each quotient level. Then $\widehat u$ is injective, $\widehat v$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}(\widehat u)=\ker(\widehat v)$, and there is an $R$-linear map $s:\widehat M\to\widehat E$ with $\widehat v\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\widehat M}$.

proof.text: Write $K_n=K/I^nK$, $E_n=E/I^nE$ and $M_n=M/I^nM$. For each $n\ge1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to the given short exact sequence and $N=R/I^n$, using the assumed flatness of its last term $M$. Identify each tensor product with its quotient using clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring]. On $\bar r\otimes x$ the identification is $rx\bmod I^nL$, so the resulting maps are precisely the maps $u_n:K_n\to E_n$, $v_n:E_n\to M_n$ induced by $u,v$. Hence $0\to K_n\xrightarrow{u_n}E_n\xrightarrow{v_n}M_n\to0$ is short exact. Evaluation on representatives shows these maps commute with reduction from level $n+1$ to level $n$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, first paragraph; Tag 00HL, exactness after tensoring with a flat last term; Tag 00DF, quotient tensor identification.

proof.text: For every $n\ge1$ set $A_n=R/I^n$ and let $J_n$ be the image of $I$ in $A_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat], $M_n$ is flat over $A_n$. Products of $n$ elements of $J_n$ vanish, so $J_n^n=0$. The scalar action gives $J_nM_n=IM/I^nM$, and the maps $[m]\mapsto[m]$ in both directions identify $M_n/J_nM_n$ with $M/IM$, and $A_n/J_n$ with $R/I$. The maps are well-defined because their kernels before taking the second quotient are respectively $IM/I^nM$ and $I/I^n$. Under these identifications the reduction of $M_n$ is projective by hypothesis: its lifting property transports across these isomorphisms by composing the given map with the isomorphism and the resulting lift with its inverse [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus [lem-trf-local-nilpotent-projective-flat-lift] applied to $(A_n,J_n,M_n)$ makes every $M_n$ projective over $A_n$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, invocation of Tag 05CG (lemma-lift-projective); Tag 00HI for quotient flatness; Tags 05CE and 05CF for the projective lifting property.

proof.text: The projective lifting property [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to $\mathrm{id}_{M_1}$ and the surjection $v_1$ of Step 1, gives an $A_1$-linear section $s_1:M_1\to E_1$. We construct compatible $A_n$-linear sections $s_n$ inductively. Fix $n\ge1$ and a section $s_n$, and form the submodule $P=\{e\in E\mid e\bmod I^nE\in\operatorname{im}(s_n)\}$, the inverse image of the submodule $\operatorname{im}(s_n)$ under the quotient map.

source.place: Tag 05D3, construction of the initial section and definition of P_{n+1}; Tags 05CE and 05CF.

proof.text: The restriction $v:P\to M$ is surjective. Indeed, given $m\in M$, choose $e_0\in E$ representing $s_n(m\bmod I^nM)$. Since $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}$, $d=m-v(e_0)$ lies in $I^nM$. Write $d=\sum_j a_jm_j$ with $a_j\in I^n$, and choose $e_j\in E$ with $v(e_j)=m_j$ using the original surjectivity of $v$. Then $p=e_0+\sum_j a_je_j$ has $v(p)=m$ and $p\bmod I^nE=s_n(m\bmod I^nM)$, so $p\in P$. Since $v(I^{n+1}P)\subseteq I^{n+1}M$, it induces an $A_{n+1}$-linear surjection $\pi:P/I^{n+1}P\to M_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, the surjectivity assertion marked details omitted, expanded by finite sums defining I^nM.

proof.text: By Step 2, $M_{n+1}$ is projective over $A_{n+1}$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to lift $\mathrm{id}_{M_{n+1}}$ through $\pi$, obtaining a section $t:M_{n+1}\to P/I^{n+1}P$. Inclusion $P\subseteq E$ induces $j:P/I^{n+1}P\to E_{n+1}$, because $I^{n+1}P\subseteq I^{n+1}E$. Set $s_{n+1}=jt$. Since $v_{n+1}j=\pi$, this is a section. To check compatibility, for $y\in M_{n+1}$ represent $t(y)$ by $p\in P$. There is $w\in M_n$ with $p\bmod I^nE=s_n(w)$. Applying $v_n$ gives $w=v(p)\bmod I^nM=y\bmod I^nM$, using $\pi t=\mathrm{id}$. Thus reducing $s_{n+1}(y)$ to $E_n$ gives exactly $s_n(y\bmod I^nM)$. Inductively choosing these sections yields a compatible family $(s_n)_{n\ge1}$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, choice of t and definition of s_{n+1}; the compatibility check is expanded; Tags 05CE and 05CF.

proof.text: For a compatible family $(m_n)\in\widehat M$ define $s((m_n))=(s_n(m_n))$. Step 5 shows this is a compatible family in $\widehat E$. Each $s_n$ is $A_n$-linear, hence $R$-linear, so componentwise operations make $s$ $R$-linear. At every level $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}_{M_n}$, whence $\widehat v\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\widehat M}$ and $\widehat v$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 05D3, passage from compatible quotient splittings to the split completion sequence.

proof.text: Finally $\widehat u$ is injective because each $u_n$ is injective by Step 1. If $e=(e_n)\in\ker(\widehat v)$, Step 1 gives a unique $k_n\in K_n$ with $u_n(k_n)=e_n$. Write $a_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ and $b_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ for reduction. Then $u_n(a_n(k_{n+1}))=b_n(u_{n+1}(k_{n+1}))=b_n(e_{n+1})=e_n=u_n(k_n)$. Injectivity of $u_n$ gives $a_n(k_{n+1})=k_n$. Thus $(k_n)\in\widehat K$ maps to $e$. Conversely $v_nu_n=0$ at every level, so $\widehat v\widehat u=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{im}(\widehat u)=\ker(\widehat v)$. Together with Step 6 this gives every conclusion.

source.place: Tag 05D3, exactness of the completion sequence, proved directly using the levelwise short exact sequences rather than invoking Tag 0315.
